arxiv-2012-05316.title: Unsupervised Adversarial Domain Adaptation for Barrett’s segmentation
arxiv-2012-05316.creator: Numan Celik, Soumya Gupta, Sharib Ali, Jens Rittscher
arxiv-2012-05316.description: Abstract Barrett’s oesophagus (BE) is one of the early indicators of esophageal cancer. Patients with BE are monitored and undergo ablation therapies to minimise the risk, thereby making it eminent to identify the BE area precisely. Automated segmentation can help clinical endoscopists to assess and treat BE area more accurately.

arxiv-2211-04321.title: Sequences of operator algebras converging to odd spheres in the quantum Gromov-Hausdorff distance
arxiv-2211-04321.creator: Tirthankar Bhattacharyya, Sushil Singla
arxiv-2211-04321.description: Abstract . Marc Rieffel had introduced the notion of the quantum Gromov-Hausdorff distance on compact quantum metric spaces and found a sequence of matrix algebras that converges to the space of continuous functions on 2 2 -sphere in this distance. One finds applications of similar approximations in many places in the theoretical physics literature.

arxiv-2212-14059.creator: Martin Bays, Jan Dobrowolski, and Tingxiang Zou
arxiv-2212-14059.description: Abstract . We study the orchard problem on cubic surfaces. We classify possibly reducible cubic surfaces X ⊆ ℙ 3 ​ ( ℂ ) X\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{3}({\mathbb{C}}) with smooth components on which there exist families of finite sets (of unbounded size) with quadratically many 3-rich lines which do not concentrate (in a natural sense) on any projective plane.

arxiv-2402-06134.title: Can 5G Coexist with Satellite Uplink in 28 GHz Band?
arxiv-2402-06134.creator: Bryce Jeffrey, Seungmo Kim, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2402-06134.description: Abstract 5G standalone (SA) rollout is right around the corner. 28 GHz band is considered as one of the main spectrum bands for the 5G SA in many countries. However, the band has already been occupied by uplink of the fixed satellite service (FSS).

arxiv-2503-03124.title: Bilateral constraints on proton Lorentz violation effects Thanks: P. He & B.-Q. Ma, \href https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/adad6cAstrophys. J. 981 (2025) 45.
arxiv-2503-03124.creator: Ping He, Bo-Qiang Ma
arxiv-2503-03124.description: Abstract Since the early reports of events beyond the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin (GZK) cutoff, the investigation of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays has emerged as a fundamental method for testing Lorentz Invariance violation (LV) effects. Recent advances in observational capabilities have resulted in more stringent constraints on LV parameters.

arxiv-2505-04206.title: 4XMM J175136.8-275858: A New Magnetar Candidate? 2026 4XMM J175136.8-275858: A New Magnetar Candidate? – 10
arxiv-2505-04206.creator: Robbie Webbe, Norman Khan, N. A. Webb, E. Quintin
arxiv-2505-04206.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Robbie Webbe, Norman Khan, N. A. Webb, E. Quintin. Magnetars are very rare astrophysical objects, with ∼ \sim 31 known to date. They are best understood as highly magnetised neutron stars, but a greater number need to be found to constrain their role in stellar evolution pathways. We apply a novel approach for the detection of fast, transient X-ray sources, using a revised version of the EPIC XMM-Newton Outburst Detector (EXOD) with the aim of detecting and identifying new and rare variable compact objects.

arxiv-2505-09591.title: Variational Visual Question Answering for Uncertainty-Aware Selective Prediction
arxiv-2505-09591.creator: Tobias Jan Wieczorek tobias.wieczorek@tu-darmstadt.de, Nathalie Daun, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Marcus Rohrbach
arxiv-2505-09591.description: Abstract Despite remarkable progress in recent years, Vision Language Models (VLMs) remain prone to overconfidence and hallucinations on tasks such as Visual Question Answering (VQA) and Visual Reasoning. Bayesian methods can potentially improve reliability by helping models predict selectively , that is, models respond only when they are sufficiently confident.

arxiv-2506-12361.title: Smallest vertical beam sizes achieved in high-energy accelerators
arxiv-2506-12361.creator: Rogelio Tomás García, Yukiyoshi Ohnishi, Frank Zimmermann
arxiv-2506-12361.description: Abstract FCC–ee aims at colliding electrons and positrons with vertical rms beam sizes between 30 and 50 nm with beam energies extending from about 40 GeV to 182.5 GeV. In this report, we collect experimental results of different high energy accelerator projects with comparable design vertical beam sizes.

arxiv-2506-23000.title: Communication via Sensing
arxiv-2506-23000.creator: Mohammad Kazemi, Tolga M. Duman, Deniz Gündüz
arxiv-2506-23000.description: Abstract We present an alternative take on the recently popularized concept of ‘ joint sensing and communications ’, which focuses on using communication resources also for sensing. Here, we propose the opposite, where we exploit the sensing capabilities of the receiver for communication.

arxiv-2508-11296.title: Unveiling the link between quantum ghost imaging and Grover’s quantum searching algorithm
arxiv-2508-11296.description: Abstract Photonic quantum technologies have become pivotal in the implementation of communication, imaging and computing modalities. Among these applications, quantum ghost imaging (GI) exploits photon correlations to surpass classical limits, with recent advances in spatial-mode encoding and phase imaging. In parallel, all-optical computing offers powerful, passive-light processing capabilities.

arxiv-2512-05995.title: The Tragedy of Productivity: A Unified Framework for Diagnosing Coordination Failures in Labor Markets and AI Governance Thanks: This is a preliminary working paper. We specifically welcome feedback and critical engagement from field experts. The views expressed are those of the author and do not ne
arxiv-2512-05995.creator: Ali Dasdan
arxiv-2512-05995.description: Abstract In 1930, John Maynard Keynes predicted that technological progress would reduce the working week to 15 hours by century’s end. Despite productivity increasing eightfold since then, workers globally still work roughly double these hours. Separately, leading AI researchers warn of existential risks from artificial intelligence, yet development accelerates rather than slows.

plos-pone-0008202.creator: Simone Wüst, Denise Tischner, Michael John et al.
plos-pone-0008202.description: PLOS ONE research article. Dissociating glucocorticoid receptor (GR) ligands hold great promise for treating inflammatory disorders since it is assumed that they exert beneficial activities mediated by transrepression but avoid adverse effects of GR action requiring transactivation. Here we challenged this

pmc-10707602.title: Rural health care worker wellness during COVID-19: Compassion fatigue, compassion satisfaction & utilization of wellness resources
pmc-10707602.creator: Bridget C. Bailey, Stephanie Cox, Lisa Terris, Dorothy van Oppen, Janie Howsare, James H. Berry, Erin L. Winstanley
pmc-10707602.description: ObjectiveThe goal of this study was to identify factors associated with compassion fatigue (CF) and compassion satisfaction (CS) among rural health care workers (HCWs) during the COVID-19 pandemic. The secondary purpose was to assess utilization of wellness resources and preferences for new resources.

pmc-11489752.title: Mechanisms of epigenomic and functional convergence between glucocorticoid- and IL4-driven macrophage programming
pmc-11489752.creator: Dinesh K Deochand, Marija Dacic, Michael J Bale, Andrew W Daman, Vidyanath Chaudhary, Steven Z Josefowicz, David Oliver, Yurii Chinenov, Inez Rogatsky
pmc-11489752.description: Macrophages adopt distinct phenotypes in response to environmental cues, with type-2 cytokine interleukin-4 promoting a tissue-repair homeostatic state (M2IL4). Glucocorticoids (GC), widely used anti-inflammatory therapeutics, reportedly impart a similar phenotype (M2GC), but how such disparate pathways may functionally converge is unknown.

pmc-11602399.title: Schwannoma of the Soft Palate: A Rare Case Report
pmc-11602399.creator: Manoj Adhikari, Kanistika Jha, Shova Kunwar, KC Sarita, Mallika Rayamajhi
pmc-11602399.description: Oral schwannomas are rare, with only 18 cases of soft palate involvement reported since 1985. We report a case of a 15‐year‐old male with a soft palate schwannoma who was successfully treated by surgical excision and had no complications over a one‐year follow‐up. Histologically, schwannomas exhibit Antoni A and B patterns.

pmc-11641916.title: Evaluating the Effect of Climate on Viral Respiratory Diseases Among Children Using AI
pmc-11641916.creator: Mikhail I Krivonosov, Ekaterina Pazukhina, Alexey Zaikin, Francesca Viozzi, Ilaria Lazzareschi, Lavinia Manca, Annamaria Caci, Rosaria Santangelo, Maurizio Sanguinetti, Francesca Raffaelli, Barbara Fiori, Giuseppe Zampino, Piero Valentini, Daniel Munblit, Oleg Blyuss, Danilo Buonsenso, Ildiko Horvat
pmc-11641916.description: Background: Respiratory viral infections (RVIs) exhibit seasonal patterns influenced by biological, ecological, and climatic factors. Weather variables such as temperature, humidity, and wind impact the transmission of droplet-borne viruses, potentially affecting disease severity. However, the role of climate in predicting complications in pediatric RVIs remains unclear, particularly in the context of climate-change-driven extreme weather events.

pmc-12471118.title: Irvine–Gass Syndrome Personalized Treatment Outcomes: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study
pmc-12471118.creator: Lorenzo Tomaschek, Laura Hoffmann, Robert Katamay, David Stocker, Asan Kochkorov, Katja Hatz
pmc-12471118.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Irvine–Gass syndrome (IGS) is a macular edema that is mostly observed after cataract surgery, also known as pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (PCME). To date, there are still no standardized guidelines for its treatment. Background/Objectives: This study aimed to compare the efficacy of local and systemic treatments on the resolution of Irvine–Gass Syndrome as well as the therapeutic outcomes of patients with known risk factors such as diabetes and arterial hypertension in order to be able to personalize treatment regimens for each patient.

pmc-12829238.title: Effect of plant waste materials as pore-forming agents on the preparation and characterization of macroporous cordierite–mullite–zirconia ceramic composites
pmc-12829238.creator: Nadeen Nasser, Mohamed M. S. Wahsh, M. S. Rizk, Gehad G. Mohamed, Omar A. Fouad
pmc-12829238.description: Porous ceramic materials have generated significant attention and played pioneering roles in a variety of industries. This work aims to prepare porous ceramic composites based on cordierite, mullite, and tetragonal zirconia (t-ZrO2), which are considered one of the most effective materials in several applications.

pmc-13107290.title: Contrasting Reproductive and Early Life‐History Strategies in Recently Diverged Octocoral Species (Paramuricea spp.)
pmc-13107290.creator: Christina Egger, Aschwin H Engelen, Roland R Melzer, Marcellina Rola, Catarina Melo, Chiara Favaretto, Manuela Quiroga‐Pérez, Sheena Suet‐Wah Chung, Lorenzo Bramanti, Ester A Serrão, Márcio A G Coelho
pmc-13107290.description: Species delimitation is central to understanding biodiversity and its conservation, yet genetic divergence among sister lineages is often insufficient to demonstrate reproductive isolation or to resolve speciation unambiguously. This limitation is especially pronounced in marine invertebrates such as corals. Their slowly evolving genomes, cryptic diversity, and complex reproductive traits can obscure species boundaries.

pmc-13220443.title: A targeted epigenetic clock for simultaneous assessment of biological aging and cancer-associated methylation drift
pmc-13220443.creator: Feng Liu, Haohao Li, Tianzhe Chen, Xiaoliang Chen, Bo Hong, Hongzhi Wang, Yeping Tu, Jinfu Nie
pmc-13220443.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAs a key tool for assessing aging, DNA methylation clocks are mostly constructed based on European and American populations and rely on the high-cost Infinium MethylationEPIC microarray. These factors limit their widespread application in the Chinese population.MethodsThis study included two independent cohorts: the Fuyang cohort (n = 610, age range 2–89 years) for model development, and the Hefei cohort (n = 188, age range 15–86 years) for external validation.

pmc-13313352.title: An integrative multi-omics approach points to membrane composition as a key factor in E. coli persistence
pmc-13313352.creator: Silvia J. Cañas-Duarte, Lei Sun, María Isabel Pérez-López, Cornelia Herrfurth, Lina M. Contreras, Ivo Feussner, Chad Leidy, Johan Paulsson, Diego M. Riaño-Pachón, Juan M. Pedraza, Silvia Restrepo, Bashir Sajo Mienda, Bashir Sajo Mienda, Bashir Sajo Mienda, Bashir Sajo Mienda
pmc-13313352.description: Many diverse bacteria can enter non- or slow-growing states where they are transiently tolerant to antibiotics. Despite its medical importance, the genetic mechanisms underlying this ‘persistence’ remain largely unknown, especially for spontaneous (type II) persistence that arises during exponential growth. To address this challenge, here we combine genomic, transcriptomic, and lipidomic analysis to explore the persistence mechanisms.

pmc-13322301.title: COVID-19 rapid testing in a homeless shelter: Lessons for equitable access and sustainable pandemic response
pmc-13322301.creator: Rebecca Ziolkowski, Jillian Kelley, Graylin Skates, Lara Balian, Tiwaladeoluwa Adekunle, Natalia M. Rodriguez
pmc-13322301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). People experiencing homelessness (PEH) faced heightened vulnerability during the COVID-19 pandemic, yet little is known about how frontline homelessness service organizations navigated the public health responsibilities that shifted onto them as broader systems strained.

pmc-13325227.title: Open surgical treatment of a 34-year-old arteriovenous fistula of the lateral plantar artery after failed coil embolization
pmc-13325227.creator: Elena Streck, Valerian Zhghenti, Christoph Düber, Savvas Savvidis, Achim Neufang
pmc-13325227.description: Trauma-induced arteriovenous fistulas of the plantar artery are exceedingly rare. Although they may initially remain asymptomatic, progressive shunt flow can, over time, result in venous hyperperfusion and congestion. Definitive treatment requires closure of the fistula to restore physiological venous circulation. Endovascular embolization is the primary, minimally invasive treatment and is effective in achieving thrombosis and symptom control in many cases.

pmc-13411953.description: BackgroundThe oncologic adequacy of distal ureterectomy (DU) versus radical nephroureterectomy (RNU) for nonmetastatic distal ureteral urothelial carcinoma remains debated, particularly in patients for whom renal preservation is clinically desirable.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies was performed. pmc-13529658.title: resLens: genomic language models to enhance antibiotic resistance gene detection
pmc-13529658.creator: Matthew Mollerus, Katharina Dittmar, Keith A Crandall, Ali Rahnavard
pmc-13529658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The rise of antibiotic resistance necessitates advanced tools to detect and analyze antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). We present resLens, a family of genomic language models that leverage latent genomic representations to enhance ARG detection and analysis.

pmc-13542158.title: Nationwide trends in incidence and in-hospital mortality of ARDS in Germany, 2008–2022
pmc-13542158.creator: Ulrike Heinicke, Thomas Jasny, Jan Andreas Kloka, Martin Scharffenberg, Jakob Wittenstein, Andreas von Knethen, Kai Zacharowski, Benjamin Friedrichson
pmc-13542158.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among critically ill patients. Recent events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and demographic changes have likely influenced its epidemiology. This study aimed to investigate nationwide trends in ARDS incidence and in-hospital mortality among adult intensive care patients in Germany over a 15-year period and to describe demographic and clinical differences between survivors and non-survivors.

pmc-13644474.title: Extraterrestrial amino acids evolve differently in asteroid Bennu and Ryugu: Possible mechanisms and future perspectives
pmc-13644474.creator: Yamei Li, Norio Kitadai, Jinfei Yu, Pengfei Zhang
pmc-13644474.description: ical processes on the early Earth, extraterrestrial delivery of amino acids from carbonaceous chondrites (CCs) or comets has also been considered a contributor to the amino acid inventory. So far, 14 types of proteinogenic amino acids have been detected in primitive CCs [1]. Comets also contain glycine and alanine [2].

pmc-13700240.title: Performance and response time in emotion recognition and mentalizing measures in patients with schizophrenia
pmc-13700240.creator: Alicia Ruiz-Toca, Alba Hernández-Gómez, Nelson Andrade-González, Cristina Fernández-Aragón, Bryan J Stiles, Emilio Fernandez-Egea, Roberto Rodriguez-Jimenez, Guillermo Lahera
pmc-13700240.description: BackgroundSchizophrenia is associated with marked impairments in social cognition, particularly in emotion recognition and mentalizing. Although these deficits have been extensively documented, most studies rely on static, highly controlled measures and focus primarily on accuracy-based outcomes, thereby limiting ecological validity.
